handoff.goals: Ensure PostHog identification is established at the correct authentication boundary with a stable user ID so browser telemetry, including errors, is attributable to the user.
handoff.did: No files were edited because `src/stores/authStore.js` already satisfies the identification contract. It identifies on successful password login and persisted-session restoration using the API's verified numeric primary key (`response.data.id`), and identifies Clerk users using `clerkUserInstance.id`. Email, name, and role are person properties only. `resetUser()` is called on normal logout and Clerk sign-out, so the next user begins anonymously. These calls persist identity in the initialized browser singleton, allowing later browser event and error captures to inherit it.
handoff.forNextAgent: Reuse the initialized client from `@/plugins/posthog`; do not add identify calls to individual event/error call sites. Browser errors captured after auth-session restoration inherit the identity automatically. The Express server currently neither imports nor uses `backend/services/posthogService.js`, so it has no active PostHog telemetry to contextualize. If a later backend instrumentation task activates it, configure a real server-side token first and use request-scoped `posthog-node` context based on authenticated `req.user.sub`, not email or client-controlled headers.
handoff.evidence: Read `src/stores/authStore.js`, which shows stable-ID identification on login, `authAPI.me()` session restoration, and Clerk synchronization plus reset on sign-out. Read `src/plugins/posthog.js` and `src/main.js` to confirm global initialization precedes routing/session loading. Searched the backend and found no imports or calls to `backend/services/posthogService.js`; `check_env_keys` confirms server PostHog keys are not configured while Vite browser keys are present. No builds, linters, or tests were run as instructed.
handoff.assumptions: The existing `loadSession()` route-guard invocation is the app's session-restoration boundary, and future browser error instrumentation uses the existing initialized PostHog singleton.

handoff.goals: Route uncaught Vue application errors to PostHog through the SDK’s centralized framework error mechanism, without installing dependencies or performing verification commands.
handoff.did: Updated src/main.js to install one Vue app.config.errorHandler after the PostHog plugin is initialized. The handler preserves and invokes Sentry’s pre-existing global error handler, then delegates the exception to the PostHog helper. Updated src/plugins/posthog.js with a guarded captureException helper that calls posthog.captureException(error) only after the existing singleton has initialized with configured environment values. This feeds PostHog Error Tracking with uncaught Vue exceptions while retaining the project’s no-op behavior when analytics is not configured.
handoff.forNextAgent: The Vue global error handler is now the single PostHog error-capture integration point. It deliberately delegates to the prior Sentry handler first so existing Sentry reporting remains intact. No build, lint, test, install, or app execution was run, per task scope.
handoff.evidence: Final targeted source inspection confirmed src/main.js imports captureException, preserves app.config.errorHandler in existingErrorHandler, delegates to it, and invokes captureException(error). Inspection also confirmed the helper guards on apiKey and isInitialized before calling posthog.captureException(error).
handoff.assumptions: Assumed the existing Sentry initialization has installed any prior Vue error handler that should remain active; preserving the handler avoids replacing its reporting behavior.

handoff.goals: Choose business-meaningful Vue user actions, instrument them with attributable PostHog captures, and record the event contract.
handoff.did: Created `.posthog-wizard-cache/.posthog-events.json` with seven core acquisition/conversion events. Added `captureEvent` calls using the existing browser singleton to: `src/views/PropertiesPage.vue` for catalogue detail navigation; `src/views/PropertyDetail.vue` for favorite state changes; `src/views/BookTour.vue` for booking funnel progression and successful requests; `src/views/Contact.vue` for virtual-assistant messages without message content; `src/views/About.vue` for successful feedback with rating only; and `src/stores/authStore.js` for successful custom login after the established stable-ID identify call. These events support property-interest, tour-booking funnel, support engagement, satisfaction, and authenticated-user dashboards. All properties omit PII and user-entered content.
handoff.forNextAgent: Browser identity is already established and persisted by `authStore`, so these plain `captureEvent` calls inherit it for authenticated users and retain anonymous browser attribution for public visitors; no placeholder distinct IDs were introduced. The direct Formspree contact form remains uninstrumented because it has no reliable client-side success boundary. The Clerk-hosted sign-in flow also has no local success callback; the custom login path is instrumented. Do not run builds, lint, or tests for this task's changes; the review step owns verification.
handoff.evidence: A source search found all seven planned capture calls at `src/views/PropertiesPage.vue:174`, `src/views/PropertyDetail.vue:546`, `src/views/BookTour.vue:609` and `:672`, `src/views/Contact.vue:476`, `src/views/About.vue:613`, and `src/stores/authStore.js:91`. The JSON event registry was read back and contains the same seven events. No builds, linters, or tests were run as instructed.
handoff.assumptions: The existing initialized posthog-js singleton maintains anonymous browser attribution for public visitors and identified attribution after the auth store's existing identify calls.
